{"session_index":1,"turn_id":"s01t02","turn_index":2,"therapist":"We can keep the exercise modest: a few sentences about an ordinary conversation, without treating normal feelings as symptoms. What would make that useful for you?","patient":"I don't know. Maybe if it helps me see that not everything I feel is... wrong or a sign that I'm completely broken. I'm so used to judging every little thing I do or feel. If I could just have a normal conversation and not spiral into thinking I'm a terrible person afterward, that would be... different. Maybe it would be useful if it showed me that I'm not always messing up, even when it feels like I am. I'm just not sure I can see it that way on my own."}
{"session_index":1,"turn_id":"s01t03","turn_index":3,"therapist":"When somebody is speaking, how do you notice the urge to prepare your own reply before they finish?","patient":"Oh, that happens all the time. It feels like my brain is racing ahead. It's this physical thing, like a tightness in my chest and my thoughts start to speed up. I'm so focused on what they might be thinking of me, or if they're about to criticize me, that I'm already building my defense or trying to figure out the perfect thing to say so they won't think I'm stupid or a failure. It’s like I have to be ready to protect myself, so I can't really hear what they're still saying. It's just this urgent need to have my answer ready."}
{"session_index":1,"turn_id":"s01t04","turn_index":4,"therapist":"Let us imagine a friendly conversation that has become a little rushed. What could you say to slow it down respectfully?","patient":"That's hard. My mind would be racing, and I'd probably just shut down. I'd be so worried about them thinking I'm stupid or that I'm wasting their time. I guess... if I were being brave... I might try to say something like, \"Hey, can we pause for a second? You're saying a lot of important things, and I want to make sure I'm really hearing you.\" But even saying that feels scary. It feels like I'd be admitting I can't keep up, and they'd judge me for it. It’s easier to just get quiet."}
